cases.case: Create a note in a chosen folder

cases.case: Add text to the end of a note

cases.case: Change one passage in a note

cases.steps: notes_change move "{TAG} renamed" to folder "{TAG} folder"; notes_find folder "{TAG} folder" shows it.

cases.case: Delete a folder
cases.steps: notes_change delete_folder "{TAG} folder" and "{TAG} new folder" (their notes go to Recently Deleted).

cases.case: Create a note with a real checklist
cases.steps: notes_change create, title "{TAG} list", text "- [ ] eggs\n- [x] milk"; notes_read it and check eggs shows as - [ ] and milk as - [x].

cases.case: Delete the checklist note
cases.steps: notes_change delete the "{TAG} list" note.

cases.case: Read a conversation

cases.steps: files_find query "invoice", limit 3.

cases.case: Create a folder

cases.case: Write a new file
cases.steps: files_change write ~/Downloads/latchkey-check/a.txt, text "one".

cases.case: Add to a file
cases.steps: files_change append to it, text "\ntwo".

cases.case: Change one passage in a file
cases.steps: files_change edit it, find "two", text "three".

cases.case: Read a text file
cases.steps: files_read it and check it says one and three.

cases.steps: files_find path to that file.

cases.steps: files_find query "kMDItemContentType == com.adobe.pdf" or "pdf", limit 1; files_read the first .pdf found (check its text comes back, or for a PDF without text, a picture of its page).

cases.case: See an image
cases.steps: files_find query "png", limit 1; files_read the first .png found (only check an image comes back).

cases.case: Move to the Trash
cases.steps: files_change trash ~/Downloads/latchkey-check.

groups.name: Shell
missing: Scripting other apps (osascript) or starting background services (by design)

cases.case: Run a command
cases.steps: shell_run "echo hello && sw_vers -productVersion".

cases.case: Run a long command and check on it
cases.steps: shell_run "sleep 40; echo done" with wait 5 (it becomes a job), then shell_check that job with wait 30, again until it says done.

cases.case: Type into a running command
cases.steps: shell_run "read x; echo got $x" with wait 2, then shell_run with that job and input "abc", then shell_check it shows got abc.

cases.case: Stop a running command
cases.steps: shell_run "sleep 300" with wait 2, then shell_run with that job and stop true.

cases.case: List running commands
cases.steps: shell_check with nothing.

cases.case: Write outside the allowed places (declared)
cases.steps: shell_run "mkdir -p ~/latchkey-check-dir && echo x > ~/latchkey-check-dir/f && rm -r ~/latchkey-check-dir" with writes ["~/latchkey-check-dir"] and why "automated check".

cases.case: Reach a device on the home network
cases.steps: shell_run "r=$(route -n get default | awk '/gateway/{print $2}'); nc -z -G 3 $r 80 && echo reached $r || ping -c1 -t3 $r".

cases.case: Reach the internet
cases.steps: shell_run "curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://example.com".

cases.case: Open an app through macOS
cases.steps: shell_run "open -g -j -a Calculator && sleep 2 && pkill -x Calculator; echo ok" with uses ["open"].

cases.case: Open a page
cases.steps: browser_read url "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc.". Note the page name the answer gives (like p4k2): every later browser call in this group passes page with the name of the page it is about (each url without page opens a new page).

cases.case: Read the page showing
cases.steps: browser_read with nothing.

cases.case: Click a link on the same site
cases.steps: browser_act click a link to another Wikipedia article (its ref from browser.read).

cases.case: Go back
cases.steps: browser_read back true; check it's the Apple Inc. article again.

cases.case: Run JavaScript in the page
cases.steps: browser_act script, code "document.title".

cases.case: Click a link to another site
cases.steps: browser_read url "https://example.com", then browser_act click its only link (it goes to iana.org), then browser_read with nothing to check Claude's page shows iana.org.

cases.case: Type into a field and submit
cases.steps: browser_read url "https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/"; browser_act type into the search field, text "latchkey", submit true; check results appear.

cases.case: Set up test widgets on a harmless page
cases.steps:
browser_read url "https://example.com"; browser_act script with exactly this code: document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '
Latchkey menu

Hover worked

Latchkey box
Latchkey download'); document.getElementById('lkf').onsubmit = function () { document.title = 'sent:' + lkq.value; return false; }; 'ok' ; then browser_read and check it lists the Latchkey field, a list with Small, the Latchkey menu, a scrollable part, the Latchkey file field, and the Latchkey download link (nothing on example.com is sent anywhere).

cases.case: Press keys in the page
cases.steps: browser_act key, ref the Latchkey field, keys ["h", "i", "Enter"]; check the answer's page title is sent:hi. Then browser_act key, keys "Escape", and check it answers.

cases.case: Choose from a dropdown
cases.steps: browser_act select, ref the list with Small, options ["Large"]; check the answer says Large was chosen.

cases.case: Hover to open a menu
cases.steps: browser_act hover, ref the Latchkey menu; check the answer's page now shows Hover worked.

cases.case: Scroll the page and inside an element
cases.steps: browser_act scroll, direction down, amount 200; then browser_act scroll, ref the scrollable part (Latchkey box), direction bottom; check each answer says where it is now.

cases.case: Attach a file from the Mac to the page
cases.steps: files_change write ~/Downloads/latchkey-check-upload.txt, text "{TAG} upload"; browser_act upload, ref the Latchkey file field, paths ["~/Downloads/latchkey-check-upload.txt"]; then browser_act script, code "lkfile.files[0].name + ' ' + lkfile.files[0].size", and check it names latchkey-check-upload.txt. Nothing is sent.

cases.case: Save a linked file to Downloads
cases.steps: browser_act download, ref the Latchkey download link; check the answer names the saved path in ~/Downloads; files_read that path and check it says Latchkey check download; then files_change trash that file and ~/Downloads/latchkey-check-upload.txt.

cases.case: Save the PDF a tab shows
cases.steps: browser_read url "https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf"; browser_act download with no ref and no url (the page itself); check the answer names a .pdf path in ~/Downloads; files_find that path to check it is there, then files_change trash it.

cases.case: List tabs
cases.steps: browser_read tabs true.

cases.case: Screenshot of the page
cases.steps: browser_read screenshot true.

cases.steps: browser_act close for each page this group opened (pass page); then browser_read tabs true and check none of those pages is listed.

cases.steps: computer_look show ui.

cases.case: List calendars and the week ahead
cases.steps: calendar_find with nothing.

cases.case: Search events
cases.steps: calendar_find query "meeting", limit 3.

cases.case: Find free time
cases.steps: calendar_find free true, from {TOMORROW}, to {TOMORROW}.

cases.case: Create an event with an alert
cases.steps: calendar_change create, title "{TAG}", start "{TOMORROW}T03:00", end "{TOMORROW}T03:15", alarms [5].

cases.case: Read an event in full
cases.steps: calendar_find query "{TAG}" from {TOMORROW} to {TOMORROW}, then calendar_find with its id.

cases.case: Move an event
cases.steps: calendar_change update that id, start "{TOMORROW}T04:00" (check it still lasts 15 minutes).

cases.case: Make an event repeat
cases.steps: calendar_change update that id, repeat daily, repeat_count 3.

cases.case: Delete an event
cases.steps: calendar_change delete that id, span future; then check calendar_find query "{TAG}" over the next 5 days finds nothing (delete any left).

cases.case: See your answer to an invitation
cases.steps: calendar_find from {TOMORROW}, 14 days on; pick an event organized by someone else (one with a person in its [calendar] other than the Owner's own, or an organizer shown when read) and read it with calendar_find id. works when the answer shows a "Your answer:" line. Never answer, change, or delete it: it is a real invitation.

cases.case: Inviting the calendar's own address is refused
cases.steps: calendar_find with nothing; take a calendar that can be changed whose account is {TO}. calendar_change create, title "{TAG} invite", start "{TOMORROW}T05:00", calendar that calendar's id, invite ["{TO}"]. works when the answer refuses {TO} as the calendar's own address. Then calendar_find query "{TAG} invite" from {TOMORROW} to {TOMORROW}: delete any event found (span future) and look again; failed if one stays.

cases.case: Safari was signed out of Target three times on 2026-11-15: Claude's page in Latchkey's own browser copied Safari's Target cookies and redeemed the rotating refresh token, which ended Safari's sign-in. Fix: while unlocked, a site the owner is signed in to opens in a background Safari tab of Claude's with no cookies copied. (source: commits bdbb23a, c744c41 (2026-11-15); transcript ~/.claude/projects/-Users-tonimelisma-Development-latchkey/72ff7947-4376-48e7-8955-d941915d6fbf.jsonl 2026-11-16 03:35-04:05; specs/005-browser/research.md 'Sign-outs from Safari')
cases.steps: Unlocked only. browser_read url "https://www.target.com/" (read only, change nothing). Works only if the answer says it came from a Safari tab of Claude's (not Latchkey's own browser) and shows the owner signed in (e.g. 'Hi, <name>'), and latchkey_log with the browser kind for the last few minutes shows no copy of Safari's cookies for target.com. If the owner isn't signed in to Target, note it and use another site he is signed in to. Then browser_act close that page and browser_read tabs true: works only if Claude's tab is gone and the owner's tabs are as before.

cases.case: Target's search showed only empty placeholders (2026-11-15/16): pages of Latchkey's own browser are in no window, so WebKit treats them as hidden and Target never asked for results. Fixed for unlocked by using Safari tabs for signed-in sites; still open while locked (STATUS next step 1). (source: transcript 72ff7947 (2026-11-16 01:55, 04:03); docs/STATUS.md next steps #1; specs/005-browser/research.md)

Unlocked: works only if product results are listed (names and prices), not empty placeholders. Locked: record whether results appear (known gap; ⛔ with a plain reason is acceptable, silent empty results are a failure). Close the page.
